exercises.title: Drone fleet fuel readout
exercises.prompt:
A small delivery-drone simulator models each drone as an object with its own fuel tank, while a separate shared counter tracks how many flights the whole fleet has completed.

Read the program in the editor and determine exactly what it prints to standard output. Give one value per line, in the same order the program prints them, with no extra spaces and no blank lines.

Every flight burns whole liters of fuel per ten kilometers traveled (integer division truncates any remainder), and every completed flight adds one to the shared fleet counter, no matter which drone object performed it.

Example: a separate drone starting with 100 liters that flies 25 kilometers burns 2 liters (25 / 10 = 2 once the remainder is truncated), leaving 98, and that flight still adds exactly one to the shared fleet counter no matter which drone triggered it.

exercises.title: Weekly reading goal tracker
exercises.prompt:
A small class tracks how many pages a reader finished on each day of the week and is supposed to report how many days met or beat a daily goal.

One line in the program below does not match that description, so the day count comes out wrong even though the code compiles and runs without crashing.

Read the class carefully and identify the single line responsible. Answer with that line's number, counting the very first line of the file as line 1.

Example: with daily totals of 20, 25 and 30 pages and a goal of 25, two days meet or beat that goal, since a day exactly equal to the goal still counts.
